pool.text: Johannesburg was established following the discovery of gold on former farmland.
Johannesburg became the headquarters of the Anglo-American Corporation founded by Ernest Oppenheimer.
The comprehensive system of apartheid racial separation was imposed upon South Africa.
Johannesburg witnessed widespread demonstrations against apartheid in response to the Sharpeville massacre.
South African Police raided a Rivonia house and arrested nine African National Congress members.
Sandton City was opened, followed later by other major shopping malls.
Demonstrations broke out in Soweto over a government decree about educating children in Afrikaans.
City Deep Terminal, Africa's largest dry port, was officially opened by South African Railways Services.
Johannesburg was affected by urban blight after the Group Areas Act was scrapped.
Johannesburg saw increased incidents of xenophobic violence against migrants from other African countries.
The Metropolitan Municipality was created and the city was subdivided into eleven regions.
The eleven regions were reorganised into the current seven alphabetical regions.
A series of riots started in Alexandra when locals attacked migrants from neighboring countries.
Johannesburg hosted the African Union Summit, which sparked international outrage over Omar al-Bashir.
The ruling ANC party lost their majority in Johannesburg for the first time.
Johannesburg hosted the 10th BRICS Summit.
Regional chair Geoff Makhubo died and Eunice Mgcina was appointed acting mayor.
The City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality had a population of 4,803,262 during census.
At least 76 people died when a hijacked building caught fire in Johannesburg.
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa launched a rescue plan to address infrastructure.
